svg.title: Step 4 · The agent and its tools
svg.desc: The chat route opens one HTTP client for the answer and builds LangChain's prebuilt agent with Gemini and the four weather tools. The agent calls the model; when the model asks for tools, it runs each call on its own, and calls the model again with the results, at most five calls in all. Each tool asks Open-Meteo's APIs, with no key, a point rounded to about 1 km, 3 seconds a try and one more. The model reads only the weather; the request and its time go to the page as the call's record. The page shows a chip for each call, running, then done, failed or stopped, which opens to the request as it went out, the input and the output; then the words, and the finished answer.
svg.text: Step 4 · The agent and its tools
One question, two rounds of tools, then the words
chat.py · answer.py: one answer
the checks, the model, the 13 rules (prompts.py)
one HTTP client, open as long as the answer
the four tools and the agent, made for it: 1.5 ms
30 s in all; each event to the page as it comes
agent.py: create_agent()
"model": Gemini, with the four tools
"tools": each call a task of its own, at once
then "model" again, with the results; words end it
at most 5 calls to the model: a sixth fails it
open_meteo.py → Open-Meteo, no key
geocoding · forecast · air quality: three APIs
a point rounded to about 1 km; timezone=auto
3 s a try, one more (tenacity); a 4xx never twice
upstream.http: host and path, never the query
tools.py · weather.py: the four tools
geocode_location · get_current_weather
get_forecast · get_air_quality: inputs checked
weather codes in words; the ambiguity rule
a failure: our sentence, as a tool error
content_and_artifact
content: the weather, as JSON: the model reads it
artifact: the lane, the request, its time, a summary
for the page only: never in the model's context
tool.call: the tool and its time, never its input
The page: a chip for each call
… running, then ✓ done, ✗ failed or ■ stopped
REST · no auth · api.open-meteo.com · 0.3 s
opened: On the wire, Input, Output
then the words, and the end with every chip
The stream: stream_mode messages gives the model's words as it writes them; updates gives each
node's result: the model's tool calls (a chip starts), and each tool's message as its call ends (the chip ends).
In the tests: a scripted stand-in model; Open-Meteo played back from its recorded answers
The model asks; the app runs: each tool written once, its failure our sentence, its request on a chip.
Step 5 replaces the prebuilt agent with a graph of our own, whose last call to the model has no tools.
